title: Linking, Steering & Summing Up
sub: Change topic, add a point, rephrase and wrap things up.

examples: In light of the incident, we should revisit our alerts.
In light of the feedback, we've changed the design.
In light of recent events, the trip is cancelled.
In light of the delay, let's update the client.
In light of the new data, we should rethink the plan.
Given that the deadline is fixed, we should cut scope.
Given that we're short-staffed, let's postpone the launch.
Given that the client is in London, let's meet in the morning.
Given that it worked last time, let's try it again.
Given that budgets are tight, we'll use open-source tools.
To put it differently, we're trading flexibility for speed.
To put it differently, the feature isn't ready.
To put it differently, we're spending too much on cloud.
To put it differently, users are confused by the menu.
To put it differently, we need a decision today.
In other words, we can't deploy until legal approves.
In other words, we're out of budget.
In other words, the project is on hold.
In other words, we need to start again.
So, in other words, you agree with the plan?

cards.situation: Giving a brief summary of a long explanation
examples: Long story short, the vendor's file was corrupt.
Long story short, we missed the flight.
Long story short, the client said yes.
Long story short, it was a config error.
Long story short, we need a new plan.
The bottom line is that we need two more engineers.
The bottom line is we can't afford delays.
The bottom line is the customer must be happy.
Bottom line: we ship on Friday.
The bottom line is that the old system has to go.
The upshot is that we can proceed with minimal risk.
The upshot is that we'll need a bigger team.
The upshot of the meeting was a new deadline.
The upshot is that costs will go down next year.
The upshot? Everyone gets two extra days off.

cards.situation: The most important part of an issue
examples: The crux of the matter is who owns the data quality.
The crux of the matter is trust.
The crux of the matter is that we lack data.
The crux of the matter is the budget, not the timeline.
Let's get to the crux of the matter.
The key takeaway is to test failure paths early.
The key takeaway is that communication matters.
My key takeaway from the workshop was to keep things simple.
The key takeaway: automate the boring parts.
What's your key takeaway from the review?

cards.situation: I'll say that in a clearer way
cards.hindi: मैं इसे दूसरे ढंग से कहता हूँ
examples: Let me rephrase that so it's less confusing.
Let me rephrase that — I meant next month, not next week.
Let me rephrase that more clearly.
Sorry, let me rephrase that; it came out wrong.
Let me rephrase that question.
I'd like to add that we also need a rollback plan.
I'd like to add a quick update on hiring.
I'd like to add my thanks to the team.
I'd like to add one thing before we close.
I'd like to add that the client was very happy.

cards.hindi: यदि मैं बस एक बात जोड़ सकूँ
examples: If I could just add one point on security.
If I could just add something here...
If I could just add — we've done this before.
If I could just add a quick note on costs.
If I could just add to what Neha said.

cards.situation: Raising a point before changing topics
examples: Before we move on, can I raise one concern?
Before we move on, does anyone have questions?
Before we move on, let's assign owners.
Before we move on, I want to thank Arjun.
Before we move on, let's agree on the next steps.

cards.phrase: Going back to your earlier point
cards.situation: Returning to a previously mentioned idea
cards.hindi: आपकी पिछली बात पर लौटते हुए
examples: Going back to your earlier point, we should log more.
Going back to your earlier point, I think you're right.
Going back to your earlier point about cost...
Going back to your earlier point, can you share the data?
Going back to your earlier point, we should involve sales.
To go back to the cost question, we have two options.
To go back to what you said earlier, I agree.
To go back to the timeline for a moment...
To go back to the first slide, these numbers are monthly.
To go back to your question, the answer is yes.
Moving on to the next item, the budget.
Moving on to the hiring update.
Moving on to questions from the audience.
Now, moving on to the last item.
Moving on to next quarter's goals.
Speaking of which, the audit is due next week.

Speaking of which, how's the migration going?
Speaking of which, the client called this morning.

On a related note, please update your passwords.

By the way, great job on the demo.

By the way, I'm on leave next Friday.
To sum up, we need more data before deciding.
To sum up, the project is on track.
